146198.why:
What I did: the word this case tells you to type, ZZLONGROW, sits at the START of the name, where a cut from the right can never reach it — so typing it makes this case pass no matter how badly the row is cut. This case’s own BEFORE YOU START asks for a match near the END of the value, so I typed Fernvale, which sits in the part of these same records that gets cut off. The Expected Results were not changed.
What I saw: work orders S2-34379 and S2-34376 come back, and the word Fernvale is nowhere on either row. The cut removes it completely. The row comes back and cannot say why.
How I know the search panel can show it: two other rows in the very same list, S2-34360 and S2-34157, do show Fernvale highlighted. So these two rows are genuinely hiding it.
Also worth fixing in this case itself: the word it tells the tester to type cannot show the problem it is looking for. A change to BEFORE YOU START is proposed separately.

146285.why: Typed a word, read the number on each tab, then opened each tab and counted the rows. They agree on every tab.

146286.why: No number anywhere in the panel reads above 20 — not a tab, not a group heading, not the “Show All” link.

146287.why: On the combined view a group shows five rows and offers a “Show All” link for the rest. Correct.

146288.why: Clicking “Show All” moves you onto that kind’s own tab, keeps the panel open and leaves your text in the box. You are not thrown onto a separate page.

146289.why: All nine tabs are present, in the expected order, and every one carries a count.

146290.why: The groups on the combined view always appear in the same order; kinds with no results are simply skipped.

146291.why:
What I did: typed a record’s number in full.
What I saw: the record comes back in the ordinary way, inside its group. Nothing sits on its own at the top.
Why that is a fail: the written requirement says an exact number should be pinned as a single row above all the groups — the “type the number, go straight there” behaviour.
How I know it is not the word I chose: I tried both the number the row labels and the number the row displays. Each brings back exactly one record, and neither is pinned.

146292.why: A record number is found whether you type the dashes or leave them out. Both give the same single record.

146293.why: A telephone number is found whether you type the dashes or not. Both give the same customer.

146294.why: A name with accents is found typed either way — with the accents or without.

146295.why: A name with an apostrophe or a hyphen is found typed either way.

146296.why: Typing the chassis number exactly finds the vehicle. Changing one character finds nothing — a typo in a number is NOT silently corrected, which is the behaviour we want.

146297.why: Typed each status word in turn. Nothing comes back because of its status. The work orders that do come back show why on the row — “Line item: approved” — meaning a line item’s own wording contains the word, which the case allows.

146298.why: A work order whose vehicle has no unit number reads cleanly — the year, make and model stand on their own with no blank gap, no stray separator and no stray word.

146299.why: A very long name does not push the rest of the row out of sight — the status marker and the second line are both still there.

146300.why: A very common word still gives a usable list: results come back and the rows are different enough from one another to choose between.

146302.why: A kind of record with no results simply does not appear as a group, and the rest of search works normally.

146303.why: When nothing matches, the panel shows the words “No results” with what you typed, and nothing else — no suggestions, no buttons, no tips.

146304.why: Opening a tab that has no results for your word gives a message that names that tab, so you can tell the search is narrowed rather than empty everywhere.

146305.why: The value finds its record. The control the case insists on was run too — a different value from the same record also finds it — so a miss would have meant a real gap rather than search being down.

146306.why: Signed in on the lower-permission account and ran the identical search. It sees a different, smaller panel than the full-access account, and no tab shows a count for records it cannot open.

146301.why:
This case is HELD by its own Expected Results — the specification sets a typing delay but no minimum length, so what one character should do cannot be judged. Recorded, not judged.
What I saw: one character and two characters both return a normal panel. Nothing errors, nothing hangs, and the second keystroke replaces the first one’s results rather than leaving them on screen.
